defaults.permitted_development: A ground floor extension of more than one storey can be permitted development in Scotland outside conservation areas where it is to the rear only and stays within the footprint, height and 10m boundary tests.

rules.height_rules: No part should exceed the height of the existing house, and taller walls near a boundary are far more likely to need permission once they start to dominate adjoining gardens or windows.
rules.depth_rules: Use a rear-only design with a footprint no larger than the original dwellinghouse. Keep total developed curtilage within the normal 50% householder limit.
rules.boundary_rules: The extension should be at least 10m from the curtilage boundary and not be forward of the principal elevation or a side elevation that fronts a road.
rules.roof_rules: The roof should remain clearly subordinate to the original house. Matching pitch, keeping the addition behind the main front building line and avoiding a bulky side roof are usually important design tests.
rules.materials_rules: Use materials and detailing that sit appropriately with the existing house.
